purpose: Per-row conformance breadth contract for docs/PYTHON_STANDARDS.md, introduced by issue #593 (Part 1 of #248). Each entry records the semantic categories a green row's registered evidence actually proves against the pinned CPython oracle, and the categories that are known-unsupported or intentionally deviating. Validated by scripts/check_conformance_breadth.py. Recording a gap here does not change the row's status; correcting statuses is Part 2 (#594).

proven.category: true division `/` on float operands
floor division `//` on int operands

not_proven.category: `/` on two int operands yielding a float
not_proven.reason: The fixture divides floats only, so the PEP's headline change -- int/int no longer truncating -- is never exercised by this row's evidence.
Operator dunder dispatch on user-defined classes is outside the scalar numeric surface this fixture covers.

proven.category: `print()` called as a function with multiple positional arguments

not_proven.reason: Keyword call arguments are rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:186, so PEP 3105's function signature -- the substance of turning `print` into a function -- is unreachable.
Same C0001 rejection of keyword call arguments at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:186.

proven.category: parameter annotations on a function definition
a return annotation on a function definition

not_proven.reason: pycc consumes annotations at compile time and exposes no runtime annotation mapping; PEP 3107's introspection half has no execution path.

proven.category: `try`/`except` selecting the handler matching the raised exception type, across several handlers on one `try`
`else` running exactly when the `try` body completes without raising
`finally` running on both the normal and the exceptional path, in CPython's own ordering relative to the handler body
bare `raise` re-raising the active exception out of a handler to an enclosing `try`
an exception propagating across a function-call boundary to a caller's handler
user-defined exception classes derived from `Exception`: raising them, catching them by their own name, and catching a subclass through a base-class or `Exception` handler

not_proven.category: `except ValueError as exc:` binding the caught exception to a name, and reading its payload
not_proven.reason: pycc does not materialize an exception object a handler can bind yet; handler selection is by type alone. Tracked by #382's remaining cluster.

not_proven.category: a user-defined exception class that declares its own `__init__`, and the instance state such a constructor would carry
not_proven.reason: pycc raises and catches by runtime type tag; the message string is the only payload the exception object carries, so a class with its own constructor is rejected with `C0001`. Tracked by #703.
A separate PEP with its own matrix row; tracked by #542, not by this row.

not_proven.category: traceback rendering for an uncaught exception
not_proven.reason: pycc emits no traceback frames, so an uncaught exception's stderr text cannot be compared against CPython's. Tracked by #606.

proven.category: `ABC` base class with an `@abstractmethod`
concrete subclasses overriding the abstract method
`super().__init__()` delegation from a subclass

not_proven.reason: The fixture instantiates only concrete subclasses, so the PEP's central enforcement behavior is not compared against the oracle.
The isinstance-hook half of PEP 3119 is not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: a class decorator applied with `@` syntax (`@dataclass`)

not_proven.reason: The fixture uses only the stdlib `@dataclass`, which pycc recognizes as a known decorator rather than applying an arbitrary callable to a class object.

not_proven.category: stacked class decorators and decorator ordering
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: non-ASCII identifiers in the Latin-1 accented range (`café`, `naïve`)

not_proven.category: identifiers in non-Latin scripts (Greek, Cyrillic, CJK)
not_proven.reason: The fixture uses only accented Latin letters.
PEP 3131 requires identifiers to be normalized to NFKC; no fixture compares two differently-composed spellings of the same identifier.

proven.category: zero-argument `super().__init__()` in a subclass constructor
zero-argument `super().method()` calls through a three-level hierarchy
`super().<property>` calling the base class's getter rather than a subclass override

not_proven.reason: pycc rejects `super().<instance attribute>` at compile time with `T0047` (#587), matching CPython's refusal to resolve it, so no fixture can exercise CPython's runtime `AttributeError` against a binary that never builds. The class-level half a `super` object does proxy is proven above.
Only the zero-argument form this row names is exercised.

rows.feature: `raise ... from ...` cause chaining and `from None` suppression (#382, #540)

proven.category: `raise X from Y` inside a handler raising `X` and reaching an enclosing handler for `X`
`raise X from None` inside a handler behaving identically to a plain `raise X` for control flow
the whole `from`-clause form compiling and running in both `--debug` and `--release`

not_proven.category: `__cause__` being observable on the raised exception
not_proven.reason: pycc materializes no exception object with attributes, so the cause the `from` clause records cannot be read back. The PEP's whole point is unobservable until then.
`from None` currently lowers to the same HIR as a plain `raise`; the distinction has to be reintroduced when implicit `__context__` chaining lands. Tracked by #606.

not_proven.category: traceback output showing `The above exception was the direct cause of ...` or its suppression
not_proven.reason: pycc emits no traceback frames, so the only rendering in which CPython surfaces `from` chaining cannot be compared. Tracked by #606.

proven.category: the `u''` string-literal prefix accepted and evaluated as `str`

not_proven.reason: PEP 414 restored only the bare `u` prefix. Python 3 rejects every combination of `u` with `r`, `b`, or `f` as a syntax error, so there is no valid combined-prefix category for a fixture to cover.

proven.category: `Enum` subclass with integer members
`.value` and `.name` member access
iteration over the enum class in definition order

not_proven.reason: Only the plain `Enum` base with explicit integer values is exercised.
Not exercised by this fixture.
The fixture prints `.value` and `.name` rather than the members themselves.

not_proven.reason: Recorded in #248 as outside pycc's documented typing subset.
Recorded in #248 as a documented boundary.

not_proven.reason: Recorded in #248 as a documented boundary.

not_proven.category: callable and generic type forms beyond the builtin generics rows
not_proven.reason: Recorded in #248 as a documented boundary.

not_proven.reason: Rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:487.
Rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:481.

not_proven.category: nested quotes and arbitrary expressions inside the replacement field
not_proven.reason: Only bare-name interpolation is exercised.

not_proven.category: underscores in float, hex, octal, and binary literals
not_proven.reason: Only the decimal integer form is exercised.
The PEP's negative half has no diagnostics fixture bound to this row.

proven.category: raising and catching FileNotFoundError, BrokenPipeError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError, and OSError itself
catching a ConnectionError grandchild via its own type and via the OSError root
a sibling handler not catching an unrelated family member, across several except clauses on one try
finally running on the exceptional path through this hierarchy

not_proven.category: errno-based construction/dispatch and the errno/filename/strerror/winerror instance attributes
not_proven.reason: Explicitly out of scope for #739 (Part 2 of #543), blocked on Part 3 of #541 and tracked by https://github.com/rotnov/pycc/issues/703; the fixture's own header comment records this and does not exercise any of those attributes.

not_proven.category: the other 10 direct OSError subclasses and 3 further ConnectionError subclasses the fixture does not individually raise and catch (e.g. PermissionError, InterruptedError, ProcessLookupError, ChildProcessError, BlockingIOError, IsADirectoryError, NotADirectoryError, ConnectionAbortedError, ConnectionRefusedError, ConnectionResetError)
not_proven.reason: pep_3151_oserror.py exercises a representative slice of the 16-class hierarchy (FileNotFoundError, BrokenPipeError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError, OSError) rather than every class byte-for-byte against the CPython oracle; the remaining classes are defined as HirClassDefs (#739) but not individually raised/caught in this fixture.

proven.category: annotated assignment with an initializer (`doubled: int = ...`)
a bare annotation without an initializer (`total: int`)

not_proven.reason: Rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/stmt.rs:195; CPython accepts it with distinct annotation-recording semantics.
pycc has no runtime annotation mapping.

not_proven.category: annotated attribute and subscript targets (`obj.x: int`, `d['k']: int`)
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: `@dataclass` synthesizing `__init__` from annotated fields
synthesized `__eq__` across equal and unequal instances
synthesized `__repr__`
dataclass inheritance with field concatenation

not_proven.reason: Field defaults are rejected with C0001 (see crates/pycc_hir/src/class.rs) and deferred to a follow-up issue.
Keyword arguments to the decorator are not exercised, and keyword call arguments are rejected generally.
Not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: `ClassName[key]` in value position dispatching to a `@staticmethod __class_getitem__`
the `@classmethod` spelling of the hook, receiving the class as its first argument
a subclass inheriting the hook through its MRO rather than defining its own
the same dispatch inside a function body, not only at module scope
instance attribute access on a class carrying the hook, which the hook must not disturb

not_proven.category: annotation-position `ClassName[type_arg]` routed through the hook to compute the annotated type
not_proven.reason: an annotation subscript is gated on the class being subscriptable (#611) but is then resolved by the type system as `Ty::Instance(ClassName)`, discarding the type argument instead of evaluating `__class_getitem__` to obtain it

proven.category: `dict` preserving literal insertion order under iteration
a key inserted after construction appended at the end
updating an existing key in place without moving it

not_proven.category: order preservation across deletion and reinsertion
not_proven.reason: `del` on a dict key is not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: a `Protocol` class with a method member

`@runtime_checkable` applied to the protocol

not_proven.reason: The decorator is applied but no `isinstance` call against it appears in the fixture, so the behavior `@runtime_checkable` exists to enable is not compared against the oracle.

not_proven.category: rejection of a non-conforming class at check time
not_proven.reason: `NotDrawable` is defined but the diagnostic for assigning it is not bound to this row.

not_proven.category: protocol attribute members and generic protocols
not_proven.reason: Only a method member is exercised.

not_proven.category: rejection of a positional-only parameter passed by keyword
not_proven.reason: The PEP's enforcement half needs a keyword call, which is itself rejected with C0001.

proven.category: `Final[int]` and `Final[str]` module-level constants
reading a `Final` constant from a function body

not_proven.category: rejection of reassignment to a `Final` name
not_proven.reason: The PEP's entire enforcement purpose is a negative behavior with no diagnostics fixture bound to this row.
PEP 591's `@final` decorator half is not exercised.
Only the subscripted form is exercised.

rows.feature: Builtin generics: `list[int]` (D-105), `dict[str, int]`/`set[int]` (D-121/D-122, PR-11a), and `tuple[...]` (D-115/D-116, PR-11b) all ship real codegen — this row's `✅` reflects all four fixtures' own CI-observed, all-5-Tier-1-target evidence ([PR #305](https://github.com/rotnov/pycc/pull/305)). `tuple[...]`'s own literal construction, `t[k]` literal-index reads, and both module-global and function-local storage are covered; passing or returning a tuple *value* across a function boundary from real, unannotated Python source does not work yet even though the codegen layer already supports it, for two independent reasons: `pycc_types`' signature-inference solver is scalar-only (D-116 point 4's correction note), and `pycc_codegen`'s `emit_expr` has no `MirExpr::Call` result-dispatch arm for a container-typed return either (D-116's own further correction note) — deferred alongside iteration, unpacking assignment, and an annotation syntax (see `docs/ROADMAP.md`)

proven.category: `list[int]` element access, `append`, `len`, and iteration
`dict[str, int]` construction, subscript, update, and iteration
`set[int]` literal construction with `len` and duplicate elimination
heterogeneous `tuple[...]` indexing with int, bool, and float elements

not_proven.category: builtin generics as annotations on nested or user-defined generic types
not_proven.reason: Only the scalar element types recorded in D-105/D-121/D-122/D-124 are supported.

not_proven.category: `frozenset[...]`, `type[...]`, and the remaining builtin generic aliases
not_proven.reason: Not exercised, and outside the recorded scalar container scope.

proven.category: `Annotated[int, ...]` and `Annotated[str, ...]` on module constants
`Annotated[int, ...]` as a parameter annotation

not_proven.category: runtime retrieval of the metadata via `get_type_hints(include_extras=True)`
not_proven.reason: pycc strips the metadata at compile time and exposes no runtime annotation surface, so the PEP's whole reason for existing is unobservable.
Only a single string metadata element is exercised.

proven.category: `X: TypeAlias = int` declared and used as a parameter and return annotation

not_proven.category: aliases of non-scalar or generic types
not_proven.reason: Only an `int` alias is exercised.
Not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: literal patterns over `int` with a wildcard `case _`
literal patterns over `bool`
a capture pattern with a `if` guard

not_proven.category: class patterns, sequence patterns, mapping patterns, and `|` or-patterns
not_proven.reason: PEP 634's structural half -- the reason it is called structural pattern matching -- is not exercised by this fixture at all; only literal, capture, and wildcard patterns are.
Unary operators are not lowered; tracked by #573.
v0.3's own Accept bullet names exhaustiveness, which no fixture bound to this row exercises.

rows.feature: `Self` as method return/param annotation (#387 Part 1) — resolves to the class's own instance type at HIR-lowering time

proven.category: `Self` as a method return annotation resolving to the class's own type
chained calls through two `Self`-returning methods

not_proven.category: `Self` in a subclass narrowing to the subclass type
not_proven.reason: Only a single non-inherited class is exercised, so the covariance that makes `Self` differ from naming the class is untested.

not_proven.category: `Self` as a parameter annotation and in classmethod position
not_proven.reason: The row's own text names parameter position; the fixture uses return position only.

proven.category: `def f[T](x: T) -> T` generic function syntax
instantiation at both `int` and `str`

not_proven.reason: The row's Feature cell names the `type` statement, but the fixture exercises only generic functions.

not_proven.category: bounded and constrained type parameters (`[T: int]`)
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by this fixture.
Only a single type parameter is exercised.

generic methods reading and writing the parameterized attribute

not_proven.reason: Recorded in the row's own scope note as single-type-param only.
Recorded in the row's own scope note as scalar-only.

proven.category: `@override` accepted on a method that does override a base method
dynamic dispatch selecting the overriding implementation

not_proven.category: rejection of `@override` on a method that overrides nothing

proven.category: nested same-quote interpolations, including deeply nested ones
single-quoted string literals inside a single-quoted f-string interpolation
multi-line expressions inside a triple-quoted f-string interpolation
`#` comments inside a multi-line f-string interpolation
backslash escapes (`\N{...}` named escapes) inside an interpolation and in the literal part
adjacent interpolations with no intervening literal text
escaped braces `{{`/`}}` in the literal part
raw f-strings (`rf"..."`) and implicit concatenation of adjacent f-string literals

not_proven.reason: pycc's HIR lowering rejects any interpolation carrying a conversion flag with an unconditional `unsupported(...)` diagnostic (crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs), so no fixture can exercise this PEP 701 grammar position against the CPython oracle today.

not_proven.category: format specifications `{x:...}`, including PEP 701's nested-interpolation-inside-a-format-spec form
not_proven.reason: pycc's HIR lowering rejects any interpolation carrying a format spec with an unconditional `unsupported(...)` diagnostic (crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs); PEP 701 explicitly formalizes arbitrary nesting inside format specs, and none of that surface is reachable.

pycc rejects `=` debug interpolations outright with C0001, tracked by https://github.com/rotnov/pycc/issues/720; the fixture deliberately omits the form so this row's evidence stays byte-for-byte against the oracle.

pycc's codegen converts an interpolation operand through the shared `to_str` helper (crates/pycc_codegen/src/lib.rs), which handles only `Str`/`Int`/`Float`/`Bool` scalars and panics on `List`/`Dict`/`Set`/`Tuple` because v0.2 defines no `str(list)`/`str(dict)`/`str(set)` semantics (D-105/D-123/D-124); PEP 701's grammar changes therefore cannot be observed over those operand types.

rows.feature: Comprehension inlining semantics -- pycc has no bytecode/frame model to "inline" the way CPython's own PEP 709 change does; this row instead verifies the one CPython-observable, statically-testable guarantee PEP 709 depends on: a comprehension's own loop variable does not leak into an enclosing same-named binding (D-117/D-120)

proven.category: a list comprehension's iteration variable not leaking into the enclosing scope
the comprehension's produced elements

not_proven.reason: PEP 709's observable contract is that comprehension inlining is not detectable from Python semantics; pycc has no bytecode or frame model, so there is no surface on which the inlining itself could be proven or violated. This is a permanent non-goal, not an unimplemented category.

not_proven.category: dict and set comprehensions, and nested comprehensions
not_proven.reason: Only a single-clause list comprehension is exercised, and multi-`for`/multi-`if` comprehensions are rejected with C0001.

proven.category: a surviving stdlib module (`math`) importable with function and constant access
a removed stdlib module (`cgi`) rejected at import

not_proven.reason: PEP 594 removes stdlib modules. pycc_std implements an explicitly allowlisted subset per docs/STDLIB_PLAN.md, so every module outside that allowlist is unavailable by construction rather than by a removal pass. There is no per-module category left to implement.

rows.feature: **Deferred annotations** — pycc reads annotations exactly per 3.14 semantics; self-referential class-name annotations in own methods work (#387 Part 2)

proven.category: a class name used as an annotation inside its own body before the class is complete
methods typed by the enclosing class and dispatched at runtime

not_proven.category: `annotationlib` and the lazy-evaluation format selectors PEP 749 defines
not_proven.reason: `annotationlib` is a stdlib surface tracked by docs/STDLIB_PLAN.md, not a language semantics category. PEP 649/749's language-level contract -- that annotations are not evaluated eagerly -- is separate from the library API that inspects them.

not_proven.category: annotations that are only valid lazily (referencing a later-defined name)
not_proven.reason: Only self-reference within the class body is exercised.

proven.category: bare-comma except A, B: catching each of two named types, alongside the pre-existing parenthesized except (A, B): form
an as binding (parenthesized form) whose bound value is re-raised and recaught by an outer handler
a 3+-type handler (parenthesized form) and a non-matching raise propagating through an inner handler to an outer one

not_proven.category: a 3+-type handler written with the bare-comma spelling (only the parenthesized (A, B, C): form is exercised)
not_proven.reason: pep_0758_except_noparens.py's three_type_handler_catches_key_error test uses the parenthesized form; no fixture exercises except A, B, C: (bare comma, 3+ types) against the CPython oracle.

not_proven.category: except A, B as e: (bare comma combined with an as binding)
not_proven.reason: This shape is rejected outright with a parser-level L0001 syntax error; HIR/types/MIR never see it, per D-195's 2026-08-24 revision note. Only the parenthesized except (A, B) as e: form is supported and exercised.
